66.d: This thatched cottage located next to the river is just perfect for amateur fishermen. It has a second floor but to get to it you'll have to use a ladder (free of charge) since stairs aren't included in the standard model of this type of house.

67.d: This thatched cottage by the river is just perfect for amateur fishermen. It has a second floor but to get to it you'll have to use a ladder (free of charge) since there are no stairs..

68.d: This little two-storey house only has one inhabitable floor since the attic has been taken over by a family of rats.

69.d: Those who like to organise huge parties will love this three-storey house. Those who do not like to climb stairs for half the day, well, they won't like it much. Probably won't come to the parties either.

70.d: This house is close to both the river and the village which compensates for the fact that it's only got two floors. Take care, though, when the river is in flood, the ground floor becomes an indoor swimming pool. If you've always dreamt of a house with an indoor swimming pool, well, all the better.

74.d: This small two-storey house is located right next to Seline and Charlotte's store and is a few steps away from the village centre. Couples who want to keep their distance will love the separate beds upstairs.

75.d: Located on the Fountain Square, this is the ideal house for those of you who like to show up the commoners.

76.d: This three-storey house used to belong to an extremely wealthy clerk who disappeared in strange circumstances. The house was left exactly as it was.

77.d: Only a skip, hop and a tumble from the nearest tavern, this house was built for people who think moderation is a distant foghorn in the mist.

78.d: This two-storey, three-roomed Master's house is clearly destined for the richest of Amakna's residents. It's big enough to accommodate several families, provided they accept to live in an community... like ants do.

79.d: This edifice has a second floor and used to be a respected bakery. Much like the excellent bread once made here, the outside is sufficiently crusty to keep out the rain and the inside is soft and spacious.

80.d: This cottage used to belong to a famous baker whose name has yet to be established. No matter, it's perfect for any Baker.

81.d: This small one-room house has the advantage of being located near the Xelor Temple and the Bakery.

82.n: Thatched Cottage by the Xelor Temple
82.d: This two-storey cottage is located right in front of the Xelor Temple and so is obviously perfect for Xelors.

83.d: This two-storey cottage used to belong to the most popular Tailor in Amakna, Elvis Trosse. He specialised in making blue pants.

84.d: Bowisse, the shoemaker, built this wonderful small house with his own hands, which makes it one of the most popular buildings in Amakna. It's probably one of the most visited sites after Xavier's Bakery.

85.d: This charming two-storey thatched cottage is often surrounded by starving Gobballs, but its location right next to a Kanojedo Temple ensures its value and interest to amateur adventurers.

87.n: Thatched Cottage by the Cra Store
87.d: This cottage used to be Edridge Valling's house before she decided to renovate the attic of her store and live there. The walls are still covered with arrow holes, but most people find that charming.

88.d: This small one-room house is very expensive because it is right next to Edridge Valling's store. Indeed, many of Edridge's pretenders bought this house to set up business beside her.

89.d: This two-storey wooden cottage near the foundry will suit molten metal apprentices perfectly. Be careful, though, the area is sometimes overrun with Gobballs.

90.d: This one-room shack is very-well located. It is sheltered from the prevailing winds and is bathed in sunshine from morning till night. That's one thing money can't buy.

91.d: This one-room cabin is on the heritage trail. This is where the famous singing Axe Smith Jony Lenon wrote most of his songs.

92.d: This one-room residence has nothing going for it apart from the fact that it was the childhood home of the famous Bowisse.

93.d: The façade of this small one-room fisherman's house might need to be repainted, although it's charming as it is.

94.d: This two-storey fisherman's cottage used to be used for storing crabs.

95.d: This old edifice has a second floor. Captain Iglout used to live there before he was given more convenient lodgings at the prison.

96.d: This little one-room shack is right by the sea. If listening to the sound of the waves day in day out is your idea of entertainment, well go ahead.

97.n: Big Hull House by the Port
97.d: This big three-roomed house has a ship hull-shaped roof which makes it an ideal Master's house. With its location by the port, you'll never again have to worry about rubbish collection day - just throw everything into the water.

109.d: This small one-room house used to belong to an old station master, Hamm Trakk, who moved out when the railway was abandoned.

110.d: This little one-room house used to belong to an old miner who used to go to work in his little train track wagon.

111.d: This two-storey thatched house is quite well fitted-out. Its previous owner used to feed the Gobballs that passed by to get them nice and fat. After a few months of intensive feeding, he'd cut their throats with his old rusty daggers. A rather strange ritual, you might say.

112.d: This small one-room house is quite sought-after. Indeed, the presence of wild Gobball flocks around makes it irresistible to lovers of Gobballs.

113.d: This small one-room house used to belong to an old alchemist who used huge amounts of mushrooms to make his potions whose effects are often underestimated. Be careful! The mushrooms that grow around this house can be dangerous and quite aggressive.

114.n: Little House near the main Square
114.d: This little sailor's house is located in a very touristy area which can be a problem for those looking for tranquillity. For those who don't have many friends, on the other hand, it could mean a whole new lease of life.

115.n: Little House near the main Square
115.d: This little one-room sailor's house is perfect for non-materialistic people who are not looking for comfort when buying a house and are easily satisfied.

116.d: For reportedly magical, but unknown, reasons this one-room sailor's house is said to increase fertility. The more pragmatic estate agents are convinced it's the single bed and the smallness of the place that have this effect on the people who live here.

117.n: Little House near the main Square
117.d: This little fisherman house is very well located, right next to the fountain of the port. It's unfortunate that it only has one room. But this means it's quite affordable for a house of this type.

118.d: This house with a ship hull-shaped roof is located near the Port Square, right in front of the fountain. For the merchants among you, it's a bargain. You'll be at work the minute you step out your door, you can save all your energy for screaming at the customers.

119.d: This two-storey house with a ship hull-shaped roof offers a wonderful view of the lighthouse. This will certainly please the romantics of Amakna whose seduction technique is to make explicit shadowgraphs with the powerful beams... you wouldn't believe what they can do with a bit of light and the human body!

120.d: This little one-room house is such a lovely place to stay that few tourists can resist the temptation to buy it. The fact that the toilets can be seen from the seashore explains why none of them stay here.

122.d: This house only has one inhabitable room since the attic was locked shut when termites invaded. Located right next to the Kanojedo Temple, it is usually reserved for the temple keeper.

123.d: This house has only one room, but you should see the size of it! It's located on an island, away from all civilization but near a bridge and a foundry. All expenses are not included!

124.d: This small one-room house has a nice little vegetable garden and is close to the seaside. This is the ideal house for any farmer who's short of money who likes to go to quiet places for their holidays.

125.d: This thatched cottage has a regular first floor, but comes with its own outhouse, which is sold separately. It's great for storing a family or two of servants.

126.d: This one-room house is close to the lake and the seaside. Perfect for amateur fishermen who enjoy both fresh and salt-water fishing.

127.d: This modest, one-room house is quite spacious and very well fitted out. Amateurs of freshwater fishing and swimmers will appreciate the nearby lake.

128.d: This cottage has two large rooms which are more than big enough to organise huge games of Tragic The Gardening... The lucky buyer will also be responsible for tending the trees in the alley.

129.d: This small two-storey house is situated on a small island making it easier to protect from Rogue attacks, for instance.

130.d: This two-storey house has a roof shaped like a ship's hull... always handy when the river's in flood.

131.d: This little two-storey house is next to the port as well as a muddy stretch of the sea. It will seduce the few crab breeders out there who don't mind having neighbours.

132.d: This tiny Fisherman's hut has only one room and as time passed by, the sea retreated from it, making it a lot less interesting. Anyway, newly weds should be happy here... at least it'll test their marriage to the limits. Then they can decide for themselves whether it's worth saving up for something better.

133.d: This house is extremely original. It has an old ship hull as a roof. This way, the owner won't have to go up and change the tiles after each storm. This house has three well fitted out floors.

134.d: This small one-room house is mainly designed for loners or tiny housemates.

135.d: This little one-room fisherman's house is quite sought after by amateur fishermen who can fish right from the windows of the house.

136.d: This house has a huge first floor you could hold the town ball in. You'll be offered a cart of hay when you buy the place. Just a little warning, however - the previous owner used to breed Gobballs and they were all set loose round the house when he left.

137.n: Thatched Cottage by the Wild Cherry Tree
137.d: This two-storey house has a wonderful oak stairway. The thatched roof along with the Cherry tree growing right outside the door give this house a very rustic style. People who want to set themselves apart from the others will just love his place.

138.n: Little House near the Wild Cherry Tree
138.d: This house has only one room... but it's huge! A magnificent Cherry tree casts a pleasant shade in the summer time.

139.d: This house might be small, but at least it has a second floor. Its location next the sawmill makes it the perfect house for the owner of... the sawmill.

140.d: This small two-storey house is located next to the Sawmill which will definitely suit Lumberjacks who hate travelling to work.

142.d: This one-room house is quite large and well fitted out.

143.n: Big Hull House by the Port
143.d: This big two-storey house has a ship hull-shaped roof which makes it an ideal Master's house. Its location next to the port means it's also popular with travellers. To be honest, though, its dark, cobweb-stuffed attic could drive a turnip to depression.

144.d: A noble house with sea view and a luxurious interior. You'll be seduced by the sumptuousness of its furniture.

145.d: The unusual architecture of this isolated house makes it extremely well-lit, not to mention comfortable. There's a splendid indoor garden on the second floor where you can go to relax and be gently rocked by the sound of the ocean.
